title: Lancashire Hotpot
subtitle: Slow-braised lamb under a layered potato crust
excerpt: Lancashire hotpot is one of Britain's most straightforward and satisfying dishes. Lamb chops, onion, and carrot go into the pot with a little stock and Worcestershire sauce, then a tight layer of thinly sliced potato is arranged on top and brushed with butter. The oven does the rest, yielding tender meat under a golden, slightly crisp potato crust.
sourceNotes: Lancashire hotpot is a working-class dish from the north of England, documented since at least the 19th century. It was designed to be assembled in the morning and cooked slowly while the family worked, emerging tender and ready by evening.

content.text: Slice the potatoes as evenly as possible, ideally to 3 mm. A mandoline makes this fast and consistent, but a sharp knife and a steady hand work fine.

items.prepNote: sliced 3 mm thin, ideally on a mandoline

content.text: Heat the oven to 170°C fan. Season the lamb chops generously with salt and black pepper. Arrange them in a single layer in the base of the roasting tin.
Scatter the sliced onion and carrot over and around the lamb. Tuck in the bay leaves and sprinkle the dried thyme over the top.
Pour the Worcestershire sauce and chicken stock over the contents of the tin.
Arrange the sliced potato in overlapping layers on top, covering the filling completely. Brush the top layer generously with melted butter and season with salt.

Cover the tin tightly with foil and cook in the oven for 1 hour and 30 minutes. Remove the foil, increase the oven temperature to 200°C fan, and cook for a further 20 to 30 minutes until the potato topping is golden and the edges are beginning to crisp.
Remove from the oven and leave to rest for 5 minutes before serving directly from the tin.

items.symptom: The potato topping is not crisping up
items.cause: Too much liquid in the tin, or the oven temperature was not increased when the foil came off
items.fix: Make sure the foil is removed for the final stage and the oven is up to 200°C fan. The butter brush is also important for colour.

items.cause: Lamb chops vary in thickness and the cut may need longer cooking
items.fix: Cover again with foil and return to the oven for 20 to 30 more minutes. The potato can always be crisped again at the end.
